mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 118i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 118i engine replacement typically costs £1,195-£2,800 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, depending on the engine code. With supply and fit, expect £2,300-£3,800 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 118i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 1 Series 118i (N43 and N13 engines) include a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, rough idling, poor engine performance, and in later stages, the engine management light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 1 Series 118i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2007-2015 BMW 1 Series 118i is typically valued at £2,500-£7,000. If your 118i is worth under £4,000, a full rebuilt engine may not be economically viable - consider a used engine or scrap the car. If your car is worth £5,500+ (low mileage, M Sport spec, good condition), a reconditioned engine with warranty is a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 118i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 118i engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old unit and fitting the replacement. Timing chain replacement alone (without full engine removal) can be completed in 1-2 days.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 118i and 120i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 118i and 120i share engine families but with different power outputs and sometimes different engine capacities. The 118i produces 127-140 hp depending on generation, while the 120i produces more power (up to 170 hp in later models).

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series 118i rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 1 Series 118i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement N46, N43, N13, B38 or B48 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 118i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 118i has been a core petrol model across three generations of the 1 Series in the UK. Launched with the first-generation E87 in 2004, it has evolved from a naturally aspirated 2.0-litre four-cylinder to a turbocharged 1.6-litre, and finally to an efficient 1.5-litre three-cylinder turbo. The 118i badge represents the sweet spot between accessible performance and everyday usability in the 1 Series range.

milestones.description: N46B20, 2.0L naturally aspirated I4, 127-140 hp, launched with the E87 five-door and E81 three-door 1 Series
N43B20A, 2.0L naturally aspirated I4 with direct injection, 140 hp, introduced as part of the E87/E81 LCI update
N13B16A, 1.6L turbocharged I4, 136 hp, launched with the second-generation F20/F21 1 Series
B38B15A, 1.5L turbocharged I3, 136 hp, introduced as part of the F20/F21 LCI update
F40 generation launches with B48A20U1, 2.0L turbocharged I4, 140 hp, continuing the 118i badge
Current F70 generation continues with updated B-series petrol engines

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 1 Series 118i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 118i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 1 Series 118i has been powered by five different petrol engines across its production life, each with its own character and weaknesses. Early cars (2004-2007) use the N46B20 - a 2.0-litre naturally aspirated unit that can suffer from timing chain wear and oil consumption. The N43B20A (2007-2011) introduced direct injection but brought timing chain guide fragility and sensor issues. The N13 turbo (2011-2015) offered more power but inherited timing chain problems from the Prince engine family. Later B38-powered cars (2015-2019) are the most reliable of the bunch, while the current B48 (2019-present) is BMW's most advanced four-cylinder petrol. Replacement demand for the BMW 118i is driven primarily by N43 and N13 timing chain failure. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW 1 Series 118i N43 and N13 Engines Fail Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain guides on BMW's N43 and N13 petrol engines were made of plastic that becomes brittle with age and heat. The guides can break and fragment, with debris falling into the sump and blocking the oil pump intake - leading to oil starvation and engine seizure. Because both engines are of interference type, a stretched or snapped timing chain can cause pistons to collide with valves - resulting in catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - rattle present but engine still running

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or engine is already damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2007-2015 BMW 1 Series 118i is currently valued at approximately £2,500-£7,000 depending on mileage, condition and generation [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Parkers market observation]. This places the 118i in the "repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit" bracket for lower-value examples. If your 118i is worth under £4,000 and the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure, evaluate scrap value first - replacement cost may approach or exceed the car's market value. For well-maintained, higher-spec examples (M Sport, low mileage, later generation) worth £5,500+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a viable investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear the characteristic rattling noise from the timing chain on cold start in your N43 or N13-powered BMW 118i, act immediately. An £800-£1,300 specialist timing chain replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. If the chain has already snapped, the repair bill often exceeds the car's value - in that scenario, compare rebuilt engine prices through EnginesMarket against the cost of replacing the car. For owners planning to keep their 118i for 2+ years, a reconditioned N43 or N13 with upgraded timing components and warranty offers genuine peace of mind.

problems.group: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear
problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear - N46 and N43 Engines
problems.rootCause: The N46 and N43 engines can suffer from worn valve stem seals, leading to excessive oil consumption. This is often accompanied by blue smoke on start-up and a gradual increase in oil usage between services.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals without removing cylinder head (specialist tooling)
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught before other damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new seals, guides and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is severe and compression is low

problems.recommendation: Oil consumption of 1 litre per 1,000 miles or more warrants investigation. A specialist valve stem seal replacement using the "in-situ" method (without cylinder head removal) is often the most cost-effective solution for the BMW 1 Series 118i. If combined with timing chain wear, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components may offer better long-term value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 1 Series 118i engine prices

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup & EGR Issues - B38 and B48 Engines
problems.rootCause: Direct injection engines like the B38 and B48 can suffer from carbon buildup on intake valves. This is particularly prevalent in vehicles driven mainly on short trips where the engine doesn't reach optimal operating temperature.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting to remove carbon deposits from intake valves
Complete rebuilt unit with new components
repairOptions.longevity: If carbon buildup has caused significant damage or performance loss

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a maintenance issue rather than a catastrophic failure point. Regular high-speed driving (Italian tune-up) can help reduce deposits, but professional cleaning is sometimes necessary. If your B38 or B48-powered BMW 118i is experiencing rough idling or reduced power, a walnut blast cleaning is significantly cheaper than engine replacement.
